title: August issue — check what stuck
intro: Eight self-check questions from the August 2026 issue.

questions.prompt: A SIF differs from a mutual fund in that it…
choices: Escapes SEBI oversight entirely
Can short, concentrate, move across assets and set redemption windows — at a ₹10 lakh minimum
Is only sold to institutions
Guarantees smoother returns
questions.explanation: Same SEBI rules as mutual funds, PMS/AIF-style freedoms, at a fraction of their ₹50L/₹1cr entry. The guarantee is the pitch, not the record.

questions.prompt: The cover story's key finding about SIFs' first year:
choices: Shorting caused big losses across the category
The headline shorting freedom is barely being used — most funds hugged the index except in Mar–Apr 2026
Every SIF protected capital in the crash
SIFs beat all mutual funds
questions.explanation: Only one long-short fund delivered 'protect first, chase second' when the market broke; early performance is a verdict on usage, not on the strategy.

questions.prompt: A life-cycle fund's defining feature is…
choices: A guaranteed return at the target year
A glide path shifting equity toward debt as the named target year approaches, within SEBI bands
A permanent 5-year lock-in
Investing only in gold ETFs
questions.explanation: One target year in the name; the glide automates de-risking. Bands are ranges — two same-year funds can glide differently.

choices: They're identical products
NPS locks money to retirement with a tax break; a life-cycle fund is an open wrapper for any dated goal with exit loads instead of locks
NPS has no glide path
Life-cycle funds are tax-free
questions.explanation: Different jobs, overlapping mechanics — the issue's conclusion is they can sit side by side in one plan.

questions.prompt: Why does the same −30% equity crash hurt less near the target year?
choices: Markets can't fall near target years
The glide has cut the equity share, so the crash applies to a smaller slice of the corpus
Exit loads absorb the loss
Debt returns rise to compensate
questions.explanation: Crash cost ≈ 30% × equity share. At 90% equity it erases years; at 25% it's a bad quarter. Sequence risk is why the glide exists.

questions.prompt: The dynamic-bond-fund audit found that median duration…
choices: Rose before yields fell — managers front-ran the rally
Rose only after yields had already started falling — the funds followed the move rather than timing it
Never changed through the cycle
Was illegal to change
questions.explanation: Flexibility ≠ foresight: the typical fund caught part of the rally, but not the early part where timing gains live.

questions.prompt: Gold doubles and your 8% insurance sleeve becomes 17%. The issue's advice:
choices: Let the winner run — it's clearly the best asset
Return to the allocation you set — trim the holding and/or cut the SIP feeding it
Double the gold SIP to average up
Sell everything else
questions.explanation: The drifted position is 'a bet nobody actually decided to make.' Sell-back is fast (taxed); the SIP cut is slow (tax-free); a written trigger makes either stick.

questions.prompt: 'Worst first half since 2020' is best read as…
choices: A signal to stop SIPs until clarity returns
A framing built to alarm — the window is selected, and the cited precedent was followed by a strong recovery
Proof that equity no longer works
A reason to check the portfolio daily
questions.explanation: Panic statistics choose their comparisons. The plan's answer is structural: continue the SIP, rebalance by rule, look less often.
